## Investigation

Which controller capabilities work independently, which depend on an official
application, and which remain unknown?

::: {.manual-prereq title="Require the investigation records"}

Review all completed records from Stages 1–7. Do not fill a missing observation
from memory, online discussion, or expectation. A missing record remains
`unknown`. Link the map to the active intention specification so its conclusion
can decide whether to stop, revise the investigation, begin learning, or open a
new software-development intention.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Create the evidence-backed map"}

Copy the template:

```bash
cp evidence/templates/dependency-map.yml evidence/records/seaboard-block-01-dependency-map.yml
```

For each capability—offline recognition, MIDI, MPE, independent sound,
configuration, persistence, backup/restore, and recovery—record status,
evidence file, and next investigation. Link only records that actually support
the claim.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Choose the least invasive next step"}

Prioritize an unknown that can be resolved by observation. Examples include a
different MIDI observer, a controlled power-cycle repeat, or a second passive
capture. Do not escalate to firmware work merely because an advanced capability
is unknown.

:::

::: {.manual-check title="Evaluate the research outcome"}

The stage passes when every claimed capability points to a specific evidence
record and every unsupported capability remains `unknown`. The map must name one
next low-risk investigation; it must not declare the device simply “free” or
“bricked.”

:::
